gloss: to argue down; to out-talk; to talk someone into submission

definitions.gloss: to argue down; to out-talk; to defeat in argument
definitions.explanation: To win an argument by talking; to silence someone through superior argumentation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}に{言|い}い{負|ま}かされて{凹|へこ}んだ。
examples.english: I was talked down by him and felt deflated.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}で{相手|あいて}を{言|い}い{負|ま}かした。
examples.english: I out-argued my opponent in the debate.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{誰|だれ}にも{言|い}い{負|ま}かされない。
examples.english: She can't be out-talked by anyone.

notes:
{言|い}い{負|ま}かす means to defeat someone in an argument.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし})
- Pattern: Xを{言|い}い{負|ま}かす (out-talk X)

WORD FORMATION:
{言|い}う (to say) + {負|ま}かす (to defeat) = defeat by saying

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {言|い}い{負|ま}かされる: to be out-argued (passive)
- {言|い}い{負|ま}かせない: cannot out-argue
- {議論|ぎろん}で{言|い}い{負|ま}かす: out-argue in a debate

NUANCE:
Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying winning through persistence or verbal force rather than logic alone.

RELATED:
- {論破|ろんぱ}する: to refute (more formal)
- {言|い}い{返|かえ}す: to talk back
- {言|い}い{争|あらそ}う: to argue, quarrel
